summary: The diff implements String.prototype.lastIndexOf in its own file, following spec steps 1-14 in order. Each step is commented, and every abstract operation is called with `?` in the spec order: RequireObjectCoercible, ToString(this), ToString(searchString), ToNumber(position). The NaN and clamp logic in step 10 is correct, including the ±Infinity and -0 cases. StringLastIndexOf is a private helper in the same file that compares UTF-16 code units and scans downward from the clamped start. Edge cases check out: empty searchString returns start, and an empty string with an empty search returns 0. There are no test-shaped branches and no made-up values. The only unreachable branch returns not-found where the spec has an assert, but the caller already rules it out. The trailing NOTE comment from the stub was dropped, which is a comment-only change inside the same function.
